diagnostic_evidence.quote: Each classification has a corresponding lower bound (e.g., \cref{sec:limit_per_lower}).

There is a dense set $\mathcal{C}\subset C(\mathcal{G},\mathbb{R})$ such that $\underline{\mathrm{dim}}_{\mathrm{B}}(\spec(H_f))=0$ (and hence $\spec(H_f)$ has infinitely many connected components, Lebesgue measure 0, and Hausdorff dimension~0) for all $f\in\mathcal{C}$.
For a one-dimensional Schr\"odinger operator, the capacity of the spectrum is always at least $1$ \cite{Simon2007IPI}, which gives a universal lower bound on the size of the spectrum.
We have developed and demonstrated provably optimal algorithms that compute various notions of size or complexity of the spectrum.

issues.failure_explanation: The demonstrated impossibility proofs alternate between a dense class $\mathcal{C}$ (spectra of lower box dimension 0) and a dense class $\mathcal{P}$ (periodic, banded spectra) to force oscillation of any convergent algorithm's outputs. This works for Lebesgue measure, number of components, Hausdorff and lower box dimension, and the corresponding decision problems, but not 'analogously' for capacity or the upper box-counting dimension. For capacity: the $\mathcal{C}$-class provides only dimension-zero spectra, and Hausdorff (even box) dimension zero does not imply zero logarithmic capacity (compact sets of Hausdorff dimension zero with positive capacity exist); moreover, the paper's own cited theorem that a one-dimensional discrete Schrödinger spectrum always has capacity at least 1 rules out any capacity-zero spectra in $\Omega_{\mathrm{DS}}$ (so the capacity-decision problem is even trivial on this class), and the swap argument cannot be adapted. For the upper box-counting dimension (and hence the box dimension on $\widehat\Omega$), the $\mathcal{C}$-class controls only the lower box dimension (=0), leaving the upper box dimension unconstrained, so the required alternation between values $\le 1/4$ and $\ge 3/4$ cannot be carried out. The prose claims that every classification has a matching lower bound (optimality), but the paper establishes this only for some problem functions.

failure_location.quote: We will demonstrate the arguments for $\Xi_{\mathrm{Lm}}$ and $\mathrm{dim}_{\mathrm{H}}(\spec(\cdot))$, respectively. The other problem functions follow analogously.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the optimality claims to the problem functions for which the alternation argument actually works (Lebesgue measure, number of connected components, Hausdorff and lower box-counting dimensions, and the corresponding decision problems on measure/components), or else establish and cite the additional dense-class facts needed for capacity and the upper box-counting dimension (e.g., a dense set of limit-periodic potentials whose spectra have capacity uniformly close to the universal minimum 1, and one whose spectra have upper box-counting dimension bounded away from 1) and give the corresponding lower-bound proofs.
issues.overall_effect: The optimality (sharpness) claims for the capacity algorithm, the capacity decision problem, and the upper box-counting/box-counting dimension algorithms under (S1) — asserted via the table caption, the 'follow analogously' sentence, the introduction's 'prove the sharpness (optimality) of our algorithms', and the concluding 'provably optimal algorithms' — are unsupported. The upper-bound classifications themselves (cor_assumI_lims, thm:box_counting, thm_Haus) are unaffected.
issues.title: Claimed lower bounds (algorithmic optimality) do not follow for capacity and the upper box-counting dimension
issues.why_classification: All computational (upper-bound) classifications and the two demonstrated lower bounds survive; repairing requires either new nontrivial dense-class facts for limit-periodic operators or a limited weakening that removes the optimality claims only for capacity and the upper box dimension, leaving a recognizably comparable body of results without new proof architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $\lim_{n\rightarrow \infty}\Phi_n(z,A)=\mathrm{dist}(z,\spec(A))$, where the convergence is uniform on compact subsets of $\mathbb{R}$.
For any fixed $n_2$, $z$ and $A$, $\widehat{\Phi}_{n_1}(n_2;z,A)$ is eventually constant for large $n_1$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof identifies the limit of the drilled covers with $[-L,L]$ minus holes centered in $G_{1/n_2,L}$, using only the lower bound $\widehat\Phi_{n_1}\ge \dist-1/n_2$ and pointwise eventual constancy at fixed $z$. But the construction evaluates $\Phi_{n_1}$ at all grid centers $w$ with $|w|\le n_1$ — a window that grows with $n_1$ and escapes every fixed compact — whereas (S2) guarantees convergence of $\Phi_n$ to $\dist(\cdot,\spec)$ only pointwise and uniformly on fixed compact subsets. No upper control of the radii at newly appearing far-out centers is available, and such holes can remove spectral points. Counterexample: $A_0=0$ (so $\spec(A_0)=\{0\}$) with the (S2)-valid, non-increasing family $\Phi_n(z)=|z|+h(z-n)$, where $h$ is a nondecreasing ramp with $h\equiv 0$ on $(-\infty,-1]$ and $h\equiv 1$ on $[0,\infty)$. At every stage $n_1$, the grid center $w=n_1$ carries radius $\lfloor n_2(n_1+1)\rfloor/n_2=n_1+1$, so the open hole $D(n_1,n_1+1)=(-1,2n_1+1)$ contains the spectral point $0$. Hence $\spec(A_0)\not\subset\Gamma_{n_2,n_1}^\spec(A_0)$ for all $n_1$, the sets are not eventually constant, and the displayed limit formula (which drops centers outside $[-L,L]$) is not the actual limit: the lemma's conclusion fails.

failure_location.quote: Since $\lim_{|z|\rightarrow\infty}\dist(z,\spec(A))=\infty$ and $\widehat{\Phi}_{n_1}(n_2;z,A)\geq \dist(z,\spec(A))-1/n_2$, $\Gamma_{n_2,n_1}^\spec(A)$ is constant for large $n_1$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen (S2) (or the hypothesis of lem:cover1) to require globally uniform convergence of $\Phi_n(\cdot,A)$ to $\dist(\cdot,\spec(A))$ (or an explicit global error bound), verify this for the construction of thm:added-1 (Dini's theorem on compacts plus approximate-eigenvector bounds at the spectral edges), and re-prove the lemma; alternatively modify the drilling construction (e.g., cap each hole radius by the finite Pasch–Hausdorff envelope $\inf_u[\Phi_{n_1}(u,A)+|u-w|]$ and round down an extra mesh step) and re-prove the two inclusions and eventual constancy. All advertised classifications survive for the intended operator classes.
issues.overall_effect: All results proved via the (S2)-to-(S1) covering step become unproven as stated: thm_warm_up2, cor_assumII_extra_lims and fractal_dim_final, the (S2) column of Table \cref{SCI_tab}, and the rigorous convergence status of the spectrum covers used in the Penrose computations of \cref{sec:examples2}. thm:added-1 (the construction of $\Phi_n$) is independent and unaffected.
issues.title: lem:cover1 is false: hole radii at grid centers of the growing window are uncontrolled under (S2)
issues.why_classification: A central lemma is false and the whole (S2) section depends on it, but the source supports a complete resolution — a strengthened hypothesis that the paper's own construction satisfies (provable by a contained argument), or a modified drilling construction with a re-proof — that preserves every advertised classification, operator class, and limit count; this is more than a routine local patch but needs no new global proof architecture and causes no major loss.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For any fixed $n_2$ and $A$, $\Gamma_{n_2,n_1}^\spec(A)$ is eventually constant for large $n_1$

issues.failure_explanation: The proof asserts that lem:cover1 provides a threshold $M$, independent of the mesh index $n$ (mesh $2^{-n}$), with $\widetilde\Gamma_{n,m}\subset\widetilde\Gamma_{n,m+1}$ for all $m\ge M$, and uses this monotonicity to exchange the $n_1$-limit with the maximum over $k\in[n_2,n_1]$. lem:cover1 provides only eventual stabilization at each fixed mesh, with a threshold depending on that mesh; it gives no monotonicity of the drilled sets in the window parameter and no uniform-in-$n$ bound (even under globally uniform convergence of $\Phi_n$, the stabilization threshold for mesh $2^{-n}$ tends to infinity with $n$). The claimed inclusion is also false in general: as the window grows, newly appearing grid centers carry rounded radii that can cut deeper into the spectral region than the cuts actually realized at earlier stages, deleting points that previously survived. Since pointwise convergence of the summands alone does not imply convergence of the running maxima (a traveling spike could persist), the displayed equality — the key step for the $\Pi_2^A$ classification of the upper box-counting dimension — is not established by the given argument. This defect is independent of, and survives repair of, the lem:cover1 defect.

failure_location.quote: \cref{lem:cover1}'s proof shows there exists $M\in\mathbb{N}$ with $\widetilde{\Gamma}_{n,m}(A)\subset\widetilde{\Gamma}_{n,m+1}(A)$ for all $m\geq M$, independent of $n$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the monotonicity-based justification with a two-sided argument: the always-valid inclusion $\Gamma_{n_2,n_1}\subset\spec+B_{2/n_2}$ (which needs only $\widehat\Phi_{n_1}\ge\dist-1/n_2$) yields the uniform upper bound $N_{2^{-k}}(\widetilde\Gamma_{k+1,n_1})\le 3N_{2^{-k}}(\spec)\le 3N_{2^{-k}}(\widetilde\Gamma_{k+1})$, while pointwise stabilization at each fixed mesh yields the lower bound; together with a routine running-minimum adjustment for exact monotonicity in $n_2$, this proves the stated limit and the $\Pi_2^A$ classification.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the $\Pi_2^A$ classifications for $\overline{\mathrm{dim}}_{\mathrm{B}}(\spec(\cdot))$ and $\mathrm{dim}_{\mathrm{B}}(\spec(\cdot))$ on $\widehat\Omega$ under (S2) in fractal_dim_final (and the corresponding entries of Table \cref{SCI_tab}) is invalid as written; the theorem's statement may still be true.
issues.title: fractal_dim_final proof relies on a false uniform-in-mesh monotone stabilization claim
issues.why_classification: A key limit step of a stated classification rests on a false sub-claim and must be re-proved by a replacement argument; the repair is contained (a short two-sided bound) and preserves the theorem, all classifications, and the advertised 'surprise' $\Pi_2^A$ result, so it is more than a routine typo-level fix but well short of new proof architecture or loss of content.
